questions.q: What problem does Data Discovery & Classification (SQL Information Protection) solve?
options: It systematically identifies which columns in a database are likely sensitive, using a built-in taxonomy of information types and sensitivity labels, instead of relying on memory or tribal knowledge
It automatically encrypts every column it identifies as sensitive
It automatically applies Row-Level Security to any flagged column
It replaces the need for firewall rules on the server
questions.explain: It's especially valuable on inherited, migrated, or long-lived schemas where nobody currently remembers exactly what every column contains.

questions.q: How does classification actually work — is it fully automatic?
options: No — it's a recommendation engine: Azure suggests likely-sensitive columns, and a human reviews and accepts, edits, or dismisses each suggestion before it's stored
Yes — every suggested column is automatically classified with no review step
It requires the DBA to manually type every column name with no suggestions offered
Classification only works on columns that are already encrypted with Always Encrypted
questions.explain: The accepted result is stored as metadata (extended properties) on the column — a human approval step is built into the workflow.

questions.q: Does classifying a column as "Highly Confidential" change anything about who can query it or how it's stored?
options: No — classification is purely a label; it does not encrypt, mask, filter, or restrict access to the column in any way by itself
Yes — it automatically enables Transparent Data Encryption on that column
Yes — it automatically applies Dynamic Data Masking to that column
Yes — it revokes SELECT permission from all users except db_owner
questions.explain: A classified column with no other control applied is exactly as unprotected as before — that distinction is the core point of this lesson.

questions.q: What system view exposes classification metadata for querying?
options: sys.sensitivity_classifications
sys.firewall_rules
sys.database_audit_specifications
sys.dm_database_encryption_keys
questions.explain: Joining it against sys.columns and sys.objects lets you generate a compliance report of every labeled column across a server.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a real compliance audit actually look for regarding a classified but unprotected column?
options: Not just whether the data is sensitive (classification already answered that), but what control is actually applied to protect it, and whether that can be proven
Whether the column's name contains the word "sensitive"
Whether the column has ever been backed up
Whether the database uses SQL authentication or Entra ID
questions.explain: A classified column with none of Lessons 31-34's controls applied is a documented gap, not a closed one — exactly what an audit surfaces.
